title: Image Generation (GANs)
motto: A GAN is two neural networks in a fixed game. One draws, one critiques. They get better together until the drawings fool the critic.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: A GAN is two neural networks in a fixed game. One draws, one critiques. They get better together until the drawings fool the critic.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Classification teaches a network to map images to labels. Generation inverts the problem: sample new images that look like they came from the same distribution. There is no "correct" output you can diff against; there is only a distribution you want to mimic.

The standard loss functions (MSE, cross-entropy) cannot measure "did this sample come from the real distribution." Minimising per-pixel error produces blurry averages, not realistic samples. The breakthrough was to learn the loss: train a second network whose job is to tell real from fake, and use its judgement to push the generator.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Generator f(z)→image, discriminator real vs fake. Minimax game until fakes fool D.
